scope_of_change.what: the thread-count source feeding guard condition 12 (scratch cap) in _a1_scope_admits

mechanism_old.proof_text: proof.md section 2 D5: 'the per-origin scratch is np.empty(max_degree) x2 inside prange; bound multiplied active-search scratch under RESOURCES: refuse when max_degree * get_num_threads() exceeds 256 MiB'
mechanism_old.mechanism: nb.get_num_threads() read inside the guard at admission time

mechanism_new.mechanism: nb.config.NUMBA_NUM_THREADS read through a tiny @nb.njit(nogil=True, cache=False) callee _a1_threads_bound()
mechanism_new.rationale: nb.config.NUMBA_NUM_THREADS is numba's configured default pool size and the set_num_threads() maximum, so it bounds the runtime thread count H from above in the same process

forced_by.finding: a direct or callee-isolated nb.get_num_threads() call poisons numba caching of every caller
probe_facts: calling nb.get_num_threads() inside a cache=True njit driver emits NumbaWarning: 'Cannot cache compiled function ... because it uses dynamic globals' and the function is not cached

isolating the call in a cache=False njit callee does NOT help: numba inlines the callee and the caller is still marked as using dynamic globals (verified with a real prange parallel=True driver and with a sequential njit driver)
the poisoning violates proof section 7.4 (no flag change: cache=True must survive) and proof section 3 ('warns nothing') — a silent cache loss on every driver, repeated per process

baking_boundary.fact: both nb.config.NUMBA_NUM_THREADS and import-time module globals are read at FIRST COMPILE and baked into the cached compiled function; the numba on-disk cache does not invalidate when the env var or global changes later (controlled probe: cache built under NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=2 still returns 2 when the module is re-imported in a process with NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=8, no recompile)
baking_boundary.within_one_process: safe by construction: the baked value is the building process's pool maximum, and set_num_threads() cannot exceed it, so baked_H >= runtime_H and the cap over-refuses at worst
baking_boundary.across_processes: residual hole: a cache built under a SMALLER H and reused by a process with a LARGER H would admit rows whose total footprint exceeds 256 MiB (bounded by CAP * H_new/H_baked)
baking_boundary.campaign_mitigation: does not occur in campaign runs: the benchmark harness freezes NUMBA_NUM_THREADS per run and pins a distinct NUMBA_CACHE_DIR per run, so a cache is never reused under a larger H; the A1 test suite likewise gives every bounded child a fresh per-arm cache directory
baking_boundary.disclosure: recorded here because the A1R reviewer must be able to weigh it; the guard never under-allocates within a process, so the failure mode is excess scratch memory, never incorrect results

dossier_grounding.quote: Compute maximum degree once from unchanged pointer data and bound multiplied active-search scratch under RESOURCES
dossier_grounding.note: the dossier fixes the RESOURCE BUDGET (256 MiB) and the multiplied-bound requirement, not the API used to learn the thread count; D5-R1 changes only that API
